findings.title: Removed grantIfNoPermission fallback changes semantics for canQuery/canView ordering
findings.body: canQuery() now calls root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_USERS) || canView() instead of previously checking canView() first then QUERY_USERS role; order change is harmless for boolean OR, but note canManageDefault/canViewDefault helper methods used by canManageByGroup/canViewByGroup chains across GroupPermissions were removed/inlined without an accompanying check that all V1 fallback call sites (e.g., RolePermissions.canMapRole) still behave identically. Given RolePermissions.canMapRole previously called root.users().canManageDefault() and now calls root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS) directly, any custom logic inside canManageDefault() beyond the role check (if present in other code paths or overridden in subclasses) is now bypassed. This refactor should be verified for all previous callers of the removed canManageDefault/canViewDefault helpers to ensure no behavior regressed, especially for V1 class hierarchies that might have relied on virtual dispatch of these methods.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission only checks root.users().canView(), ignoring canManage()
findings.body: Previously (per the diff), the old getGroupsWithViewPermission() method checked both canView() and canManage() of root.users() before returning empty set. The new getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() only checks root.users().canView(). This means an admin with only manage permission on users (but not explicit view) will now have groups incorrectly filtered/computed, which could result in incorrect scoping or performance overhead from needlessly computing group IDs when the admin should already have full access via manage permission.

findings.title: searchForUser no longer checks canView() before computing/filtering groupIds, double filtering removed
findings.body: The old code wrapped the groupIds lookup in `if (!auth.users().canView())`, avoiding unnecessary computation of group IDs for admins who can already view all users, and separately filtered the stream with `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`. The new code unconditionally computes `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (which internally checks canView() so it's not functionally broken) and removes the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` on the stream from `searchForUserStream`, instead relying solely on `toRepresentation`'s filter. This refactor is likely fine functionally, but removing the direct filtering here is a behavior-sensitive change that should be covered by tests ensuring per-user permission filtering still works correctly when group-based attribute injection (UserModel.GROUPS session attribute) is used with searchForUserStream, since the underlying store query uses the GROUPS session attribute for filtering, and if that store-level filtering has gaps, results could leak un-permitted users without an additional in-memory filter safety net.

findings.title: canManage(UserModel) role check changed from ADMIN+MANAGE_USERS to only MANAGE_USERS
findings.body: The diff removes AdminRoles.ADMIN from the hasOneAdminRole() check in canView(UserModel) and canManage(UserModel). This could change authorization behavior for callers previously granted access via the generic ADMIN role; if ADMIN role holders are expected to always have access, this is a regression that should be confirmed as intentional (schema cleanup) and covered by a test.
